newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr seen trading sideways after tumbling.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr seen trading sideways after tumbling.

text.p: The dollar will likely consolidate in the short run after tumbling briefly below 120 yen, chartists said.
On Friday, the ailing greenback nosedived more than two yen to 119.10 yen, its lowest level since late January.
The dollar, however, trimmed its losses to hover above 120 yen in late afternoon trading.
"Now, we are going to begin a fourth wave consolidation," said Joseph Klettner, a foreign exchange technical analyst at Chase Securities Inc.

"And this consolidation should take a long time because we moved so far in such a short period of time that we have to now move sideways for a considerable period of time to make up for that," Klettner said.
On the upside, the dollar should stall between 121.49 yen and 122.98 yen, according to Klettner.
He noted that 121.49 yen is a 38.2 percent Fibonacci retracement of the third wave that began from 125.36 on Thursday and bottomed at 119.10 on Friday.
Klettner deemed 122.98 yen represented a 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement of the third wave.
After working its way higher, Klettner said the dollar should retest the bottom of the third wave at 119.10 yen.
This move could be followed by another bounce up to the area between 121.49 yen and 122.98, he said.

The dollar's rollercoaster ride on Friday reflected a reversal in expectations for official U.S. and Japanese interest rates as well as repeated jawboning by Japanese officials for deflating the dollar.
The beleaguered U.S. currency closed at 120.20/30 yen, down from 121.95/00 at the open.
Foreign Exchange Analytics Partner David Solin agreed that the market does need time to "digest" the moves on Friday.
However, he warned that Japanese players returning on Monday may try to push the dollar even lower.
"If it does break lower, I don't think we'll see a lot lower of a market," Solin said.
As for how far down the dollar might fall on Monday, Solin targeted 118.50 yen, which he called a 38 percent Fibonacci retracement from 103.85, the low from May of 1996.
